headline: 207 caps, 125 goals: Messi retires from international football
summary: The 39-year-old legend calls time on his remarkable career with Argentina, leaving a legacy that David Beckham says 'will live forever'.
details: Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football after a storied career with Argentina. The 39-year-old forward earned 207 caps and scored 125 goals for his national team.
Messi's international journey reached its pinnacle with the 2022 World Cup victory in Qatar. His final appearance for Argentina was in the World Cup final defeat against Spain in July.
Former England captain David Beckham praised the legend, stating that Messi's legacy 'will live forever' and that he provided the 'greatest gift' to his country.
Beckham, now a co-owner of Messi's current club Inter Miami, highlighted how Messi's talent and humility have inspired millions of children worldwide.
FIFA President Gianni Infantino also hailed Messi's 'extraordinary' career, noting that his magical talent will be remembered forever.
caption:
207 caps and 125 goals. The end of an era as Lionel Messi bids farewell to Argentina.

Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football after a storied career with Argentina. The 39-year-old forward earned 207 caps and scored 125 goals for his national team.

Messi's international journey reached its pinnacle with the 2022 World Cup victory in Qatar. His final appearance for Argentina was in the World Cup final defeat against Spain in July.

Former England captain David Beckham praised the legend, stating that Messi's legacy 'will live forever' and that he provided the 'greatest gift' to his country.

Beckham, now a co-owner of Messi's current club Inter Miami, highlighted how Messi's talent and humility have inspired millions of children worldwide.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino also hailed Messi's 'extraordinary' career, noting that his magical talent will be remembered forever.

headline: 1,324 new cases: 5 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The total death toll has reached 102 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
details: Five people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 102 this year, according to a DGHS notice on Tuesday.
A total of 1,324 new patients were recorded in the same period, pushing the total number of hospitalizations for dengue this year to 37,170.
The distribution of new hospitalizations shows the highest burden in the Dhaka division with 578 patients, followed by Khulna with 246 and Chattogram with 139.
Other affected regions include Rajshahi (114), Barishal (121), Mymensingh (87), Rangpur (34), and Sylhet (5).
caption:
1,324 new cases in just 24 hours. Dengue deaths in Bangladesh have now reached 102.

Five people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 102 this year, according to a DGHS notice on Tuesday.

A total of 1,324 new patients were recorded in the same period, pushing the total number of hospitalizations for dengue this year to 37,170.

The distribution of new hospitalizations shows the highest burden in the Dhaka division with 578 patients, followed by Khulna with 246 and Chattogram with 139.

Other affected regions include Rajshahi (114), Barishal (121), Mymensingh (87), Rangpur (34), and Sylhet (5).
